master_plan_principles_consumed.principle_text: Runtime resolver handoff proceeds to the concurrent replay/paper input-lock gate; replay and paper are separate concurrent lanes after the shared input lock.
Replay and paper are separate lanes; replay passing into paper as a sequential transition is not the Stage-1 pre-live validation policy.
Replay and paper result packets remain separate static boundary concepts and are not merged into live or owner approval proof by PR #90.
The pre-live validation consumer is concurrent replay/paper only where the master plan defines it, with no direct dual review, owner review, canary, live, or day-one authority.
PR #90 is a static competition gate; replay and paper execution remain later runtime concerns.
Replay/paper result packets are later runtime artifacts and PR #90 references only result boundary contracts.
Dual-result review remains a later PR #91 consumer and is not created by PR #90.
Owner live-promotion review remains a later PR #92 gate and is not created by PR #90.
edge_hypothesis_packet_required_before_parameter_stack_selection_flag = true.
edge_parameter_stack_selection_required_flag = true.
Selected parameter-stack handoff remains static until later gates and cannot become order, replay, paper, or live authority.
AtomicRows is parameter inventory, not a trader or source of live authority.
Single-parameter or single-algorithm trade selection is forbidden; QTT uses role-complete parameter stacks.
Required stack roles include SIGNAL, SCORING, NORMALIZATION, RISK, EXECUTION, CAPITAL, LATENCY, ERROR_GUARD, and repo-required QUANTUM_ADVISORY.
Blocked, source-missing, negative, unknown, owner-pending, rejected, or dormant rows are excluded from active selected stacks and may appear only as blocked diagnostics.
Quantum optimizers may rank or refine candidate stack ordering but cannot become direct live order authority.
Classical execution gates remain final for execution release, and the live decision chain reaches execution routing only after upstream gates.
Execution Router remains the final order-submission authority; this static competition packet creates no order authority.
Source, connector, runtime cash, order, and fill facts require accepted-source or runtime receipts where policy requires them; PR #90 creates none.
Owner review and owner approval are later gates and are not created by this static packet.

Do not invent parameter values, ranges, defaults, source claims, optimizer defaults, broker settings, venue rules, financial constants, quantum backend values, owner assignments, code paths, runtime receipts, replay/paper results, test pass claims, AtomicRows bundle creation, or zip ingestion success.
